Window-based Transition Network Analysis

Source: R/wtna.R
wtna.Rd

wtna() builds a network from one-hot data, where each row is a time point and each code column holds 1 when that code is active, by counting codes across windows of consecutive rows. It returns a directed transition network (codes active in one window, followed by codes active in the next), an undirected co-occurrence network (codes active in the same window), or both. With actor, each actor's rows are counted on their own and the counts summed, so no window spans two actors. The networks are the ones build_network(method = "wtna") and build_network(method = "wtna_cooccurrence") estimate.

The weights count pairs of active codes, not events: a row with several active codes adds to several edges at once, and a larger window pairs more rows. Compare networks built with the same window_size and mode. How far the weights move under resampling of actors is checked with bootstrap_network(), and two networks are compared with permutation(); both need actor, since rows without it form a single unit.

Usage

wtna(
  data,
  method = c("transition", "cooccurrence", "both"),
  type = c("frequency", "relative"),
  codes = NULL,
  window_size = 3L,
  mode = c("non-overlapping", "overlapping"),
  actor = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'wtna_mixed'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

data

A data frame or matrix whose rows are time points, in order, holding the one-hot code columns and, optionally, the actor column. A column named in codes may hold only 0, 1 or missing; a missing cell counts as inactive, and any other value raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input. Under the default codes = NULL such a column is not read as a code.

method

The network to build: "transition" (default), directed, from the codes of one window to those of the next; "cooccurrence", undirected, between the codes of the same window; or "both", which returns the two networks together as a wtna_mixed.

type

The weights: "frequency" (default) keeps the counts, and "relative" divides each row by its sum (a row without counts stays zero). On a co-occurrence network "relative" gives an asymmetric matrix, the co-occurrence conditional on the row's code, so keep "frequency" when symmetric counts are needed.

codes

The one-hot columns, as names, as column positions, or as a single "first:last" string naming a range of adjacent columns. Default NULL, every numeric or logical column holding only 0, 1 and missing values, except actor. At least two codes are needed, and a name that is not a column stops wtna().

window_size

The number of consecutive rows in a window, a whole number of at least 1. Default 3. With 1 there is no windowing: transitions are counted from each row to the next, and co-occurrence within each row, and mode is ignored.

mode

How windows are formed when window_size is above 1. "non-overlapping" (default) cuts the rows into consecutive, separate blocks of window_size rows. "overlapping" first replaces the rows by one row per sliding window of window_size rows (step 1), marking a code active when it is active in any of them, so n rows give n - window_size + 1 windows, and then counts those in blocks of window_size, as tna::import_onehot(window_type = "sliding") does.

actor

The column, or columns, naming who each row belongs to. The counts are computed per actor (per combination of values, for several columns) and summed. Default NULL, all rows as one sequence. A missing identifier raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input, and a name that is not a column stops wtna(). With several columns, the initial-state distribution groups the rows by the first column only.

x

For the print() method: a wtna_mixed object.

...

For the print() method: ignored.

Value

For method = "transition" or "cooccurrence": a netobject (class c("netobject", "cograph_network"), see build_network()) with method set to "wtna_transition" or "wtna_cooccurrence". print() shows the weights and, for transitions, the initial probabilities; extract_edges() gives one row per edge, extract_initial_probs() the initial-state distribution of a transition network, cograph::splot() draws it, bootstrap_network() resamples its actors, and permutation() compares it with a second network by permuting actors. It is directed only for transitions, holds the input as given in data, and records the windowing settings (type, window_size, mode, codes, actor) in params. A transition network also stores the initial-state distribution in initial: for each actor (the first actor column when there are several), the codes active in its first row with an active code share its weight equally, and the shares are averaged over actors (without actor, the first row with an active code in the whole data).

For method = "both": a wtna_mixed object, a list of the transition and cooccurrence networks (each a netobject as above) and method = "wtna_both". Its print() gives the node and edge counts of each network and returns its input invisibly; bootstrap_network() and permutation() test both networks.

Details

Transitions: with window_size = 1, crossprod(X[-n, ], X[-1, ]) counts how often code i is active in row t and code j in row t + 1. With larger windows, every row of a window is paired with every row of the next window, which is the outer product of the two windows' column sums; a final, shorter window is counted as the successor of the last full one.

Co-occurrence: with window_size = 1, crossprod(X) counts the codes active in the same row, so the diagonal is how often each code is active. With larger windows, every row of a window is paired with every row of the same window, itself included, which is the outer product of the window's column sums.

Windows: in non-overlapping windows a code counts once for each row it is active in. These counts follow tna's windowed algorithm.

Per actor: with actor, the counts are computed per group and summed.

See also

build_network

Examples

oh <- matrix(c(1,0,0, 0,1,0, 0,0,1, 1,0,0), nrow = 4, byrow = TRUE,
             dimnames = list(NULL, c("A","B","C")))
w <- wtna(oh)

# \donttest{
# Simple one-hot data
df <- data.frame(
  A = c(1, 0, 1, 0, 1),
  B = c(0, 1, 0, 1, 0),
  C = c(0, 0, 1, 0, 0)
)

# Transition network
net <- wtna(df)
print(net)
#> Network (method: wtna_transition) [directed]
#>   Weights: [1.000, 2.000]  |  mean: 1.333
#> 
#>   Weight matrix:
#>     A B C
#>   A 2 2 0
#>   B 1 1 0
#>   C 1 1 0 
#> 
#>   Initial probabilities:
#>   A             1.000  ████████████████████████████████████████
#>   B             0.000  
#>   C             0.000  

# Both networks
nets <- wtna(df, method = "both")
print(nets)   # the transition and the co-occurrence network
#> Mixed Window TNA (transition + co-occurrence)
#> -- Transition (directed) --
#>   Nodes: 3  |  Edges: 6
#> -- Co-occurrence (undirected) --
#>   Nodes: 3  |  Edges: 6

# With windowing
net <- wtna(df, window_size = 2, mode = "non-overlapping")
# }
